# Option premium execution gate

This document defines the money path that must exist before h/monhook options can accept real SOL. The development contract collects premiums in a separate system-owned PDA, allows a constrained Pump curve buyback after sellout, and lets buyers reclaim unspent premiums after expiry. The Pump route has passed local-validator tests with a test double and a dump of Pump's deployed mainnet SBF. The latter confirms instruction compatibility and exact premium balance reduction, but uses a manually selected strike and does not cover migrated PumpSwap pools. A post-migration route, funded devnet deployment and independent review are still required. The frontend must keep option purchases unavailable until those gates pass.

## Owner decision

When a sold-out series uses premiums to buy back its Mint, the acquired tokens go into a program-owned token vault with no issuer withdrawal path. They are not credited to the issuer or to an operator wallet. This vault must be distinct from the collateral vault used to pay option claims.

## Required accounting

- Account for series rent and the separate buyback PDA rent reserve apart from premiums. At every state transition, recorded unspent premiums must be backed by lamports above that rent reserve.
- Track total premium received, amount committed to completed buybacks, amount refunded, and remaining balance. A retry cannot spend or refund the same lamports twice. The development contract now records successful Pump-route spending and post-expiry claims, and returns the rent reserve to the issuer only after the premium balance reaches zero.
- A buyback is eligible only after `sold_lots == total_lots`. It must use an explicitly allowed on-chain venue, the series Mint, a bounded SOL input, a committed minimum token output, and the immutable buyback vault as destination.
- The program must compare custody balances before and after the market CPI. It must reject a zero-output purchase, excess SOL spend, changed destination, unrelated token Mint, arbitrary program invocation, and any attempt to drain collateral.
- If no supported market route can execute by expiry, each buyer can claim a proportional share of unspent premiums after expiry, even if their option was exercised or the series defaulted. The final buyer claim receives any integer-rounding remainder. The current local-validator test covers this fallback without a prior buyback. A future route must stop spending at expiry and preserve the same accounting invariant.
- No issuer, operator, upgrade authority, or keeper withdrawal may bypass these rules. A keeper may submit a transaction and pay its own network fee but may not receive premium principal or bought tokens.

## Route implementation notes

- The collateral vault is already the Token-2022 associated account owned by the series PDA. It cannot also be the permanent buyback destination. Derive a separate buyback authority PDA from the series and use its Token-2022 associated account for acquired tokens. No instruction may transfer tokens out of that account. The final program upgrade authority must be addressed before calling it permanently unwithdrawable.
- `options-client.mjs` derives this separate PDA and its token accounts, builds the Pump curve-buy CPI account list, and validates the installed SDK's generated route. For SOL-paired Pump trades, the wrapped-SOL ATA is passed as an address but not used or created; the buyer PDA pays with native SOL. The preparation helper creates only the Token-2022 destination ATA. The options program now invokes this route after checking the official program, Mint, vault, fee recipient, exact quote budget and minimum output.
- For a token still trading on its Pump bonding curve, the official `buy_exact_quote_in_v3` instruction accepts an exact quote input and minimum base-token output with 17 accounts. Build and pin its instruction data and account layout, require the official Pump program, the series Mint, Token-2022, wrapped SOL, the distinct buyback authority and its own token account. The series program must measure the quote spent and tokens received across the CPI, enforce a price ceiling derived from published series terms, and preserve all unspent premium for refunds. The SDK document is [Pump Bonding Curve Trades V3](https://github.com/pump-fun/pump-public-docs/blob/main/docs/instructions/TRADE_V3.md).
- A migrated token requires a separate, equally constrained PumpSwap route. Pump's [PumpSwap Trades V2](https://github.com/pump-fun/pump-public-docs/blob/main/docs/instructions/PUMP_SWAP_TRADE_V2.md) documents the post-migration instruction family. Unlike the Pump curve route, a SOL-paired PumpSwap trade requires a real wrapped-SOL token account for the PDA buyer. The program must create/fund and sync that account, validate the pool's Mint/vaults, account for its rent separately, check exact quote consumption, and close or recover its rent after settlement. A bonding-curve failure must never cause a keeper to receive premium SOL directly. If neither verified route executes before expiry, the current refund instruction remains available.
- The issuer funds the buyer PDA's zero-data rent reserve when opening the series. A keeper supplies a bounded temporary SOL top-up for any Pump-created user volume account rent (currently 0.0018444 SOL when missing) and bonding-curve rent top-up; the program refunds any unused top-up after the CPI. It checks that the PDA retains its original balance minus the exact premium spend, so the keeper cannot receive premium principal. The unused wrapped-SOL ATA is not created. A local test using Pump's deployed SBF checked that the premium balance fell by exactly 10,000,000 lamports while purchased tokens reached the permanent vault.

## Release evidence

1. Local-validator tests cover partial sale, sold-out eligibility, a successful buyback, slippage rejection, a venue migration or unavailable route, refund fallback, concurrent/repeated calls, default, exercise, expiry, and invariant preservation after failed CPI.
2. A funded devnet deployment repeats the full sequence with real signed transactions and independently inspectable program accounts.
3. An independent review examines both program binaries, the SDK transaction builder, and the exact supported market route before mainnet options are enabled.

The local-validator test double exercised sellout eligibility, a successful CPI buy, a substituted-vault rejection, a too-low output rejection, overspend rejection, post-expiry premium refund and final rent return. A separate local-validator test loaded Pump's actual deployed SBF, cloned its mainnet global and fee accounts, created a Token-2022 Pump coin, bought collateral, opened and sold out a 2%-supply option series, then executed a 10,000,000-lamport buyback. The premium PDA balance fell from 200,890,880 to 190,890,880 lamports and the permanent vault received 310,858,132,043 base units. This tests a local fork of chain state, not funded devnet or mainnet, and does not cover migrated PumpSwap pools. Funded devnet and independent-review gates remain closed.

The real-program test is reproducible with `scripts/test-options-pump-real-local.mjs` against a local validator that loads the SBF dumped from Pump's deployed program ID `6EF8r…F6P`, the newly built options SBF, and clones Pump global `4wTV1…xnjf`, Pump fee config `8Wf5T…Tt`, and the chosen buyback fee recipient `5YxQF…eD` from mainnet. The test uses disposable local wallets and local airdrops only. The program binary is a read-only local test artifact and is not committed to this repository.
